blocks.alt: Glowing glass sauna in the forest at night as steam rises from the stones, The Toronto Sauna Co.

blocks.text: Wellness & lifestyle
Heat. Quiet. Ritual.

blocks.html: The traditional Finnish sauna is one of the oldest wellness practices on earth, and one of the best studied. Here is what the research says, and why so many people make it the best part of their day.
blocks.text: The traditional Finnish sauna is one of the oldest wellness practices on earth, and one of the best studied. Here is what the research says, and why so many people make it the best part of their day.

blocks.text: What the research says How to sauna
The Finnish tradition
Real heat. Real steam.

blocks.html: In Finland, the sauna isn’t a luxury. It’s part of everyday life. The country has roughly three million saunas for about five and a half million people, and in 2020 Finnish sauna culture was added to UNESCO’s list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
blocks.text: In Finland, the sauna isn’t a luxury. It’s part of everyday life. The country has roughly three million saunas for about five and a half million people, and in 2020 Finnish sauna culture was added to UNESCO’s list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

blocks.html: A true Finnish sauna is a dry, wood-lined room heated to about 80–100°C by a stove full of hot rocks. Ladle a little water on the stones and you get löyly: a soft wave of steam that rolls over you and makes the heat feel deeper. It’s the heat the research is built on, and it’s the heat every one of our saunas is designed around.

blocks.text: What the research says
The science of sweat.

blocks.html: Much of the best-known research comes from Finland, where researchers followed more than 2,300 middle-aged men for about 20 years and compared how often they used the sauna. The findings are striking.
blocks.text: Much of the best-known research comes from Finland, where researchers followed more than 2,300 middle-aged men for about 20 years and compared how often they used the sauna. The findings are striking.

blocks.html: Lower risk of death from any cause
blocks.text: Lower risk of death from any cause

blocks.html: Men who used the sauna 4–7 times a week had about a 40% lower risk of death from any cause over 20 years than men who went once a week.
blocks.text: Men who used the sauna 4–7 times a week had about a 40% lower risk of death from any cause over 20 years than men who went once a week.
JAMA Internal Medicine, 2015

blocks.html: Lower risk of sudden cardiac death
blocks.text: Lower risk of sudden cardiac death

blocks.html: The same frequent sauna users had a 63% lower risk of sudden cardiac death. Even 2–3 sessions a week was linked to a 22% lower risk.
blocks.text: The same frequent sauna users had a 63% lower risk of sudden cardiac death. Even 2–3 sessions a week was linked to a 22% lower risk.
JAMA Internal Medicine, 2015
Lower risk of dementia

blocks.html: In the same group of men, those who used the sauna 4–7 times a week were about 66% less likely to be diagnosed with dementia.
blocks.text: In the same group of men, those who used the sauna 4–7 times a week were about 66% less likely to be diagnosed with dementia.
Age and Ageing, 2017
Studies reviewed

blocks.html: A Mayo Clinic Proceedings review of more than 70 studies linked regular Finnish sauna use with lower blood pressure, healthier blood vessels and less inflammation.
blocks.text: A Mayo Clinic Proceedings review of more than 70 studies linked regular Finnish sauna use with lower blood pressure, healthier blood vessels and less inflammation.
Mayo Clinic Proceedings, 2018
Reported better sleep

blocks.html: In a global survey of regular sauna users, 84% said they slept better for one to two nights after a session.
blocks.text: In a global survey of regular sauna users, 84% said they slept better for one to two nights after a session.
Global Sauna Survey, 2019
Reason people sauna: to de-stress

blocks.html: Every respondent in the same survey rated relaxation and stress relief as a key reason they use the sauna. People who went 5–15 times a month reported higher mental well-being.
blocks.text: Every respondent in the same survey rated relaxation and stress relief as a key reason they use the sauna. People who went 5–15 times a month reported higher mental well-being.
Global Sauna Survey, 2019

blocks.html: These are observational studies: they show strong associations, not proof that the sauna alone caused the results, and most of the long-term data comes from Finnish men. Sauna is a wonderful habit, not a medical treatment. Sources are listed at the bottom of this page.

blocks.text: The lifestyle

blocks.html: More than health. A way of living.
blocks.text: More than health. A way of living.

blocks.html: The numbers are compelling, but that isn’t why people fall in love with sauna. They fall in love with how it feels, and with what it does to the rhythm of their day.
blocks.text: The numbers are compelling, but that isn’t why people fall in love with sauna. They fall in love with how it feels, and with what it does to the rhythm of their day.

blocks.alt: Cedar and black sauna on a stone patio with fire pit at golden hour, The Toronto Sauna Co.

blocks.html: A daily resetTwenty minutes of heat with no phone, no screen and nowhere to be. For many people it’s the only truly quiet part of the day.
blocks.text: A daily resetTwenty minutes of heat with no phone, no screen and nowhere to be. For many people it’s the only truly quiet part of the day.

blocks.html: The spa, at homeNo membership, no drive, no booking. Your own sauna is ready whenever you are: before work, after a run, or under the stars on a January night.

blocks.html: Time togetherSauna has always been social. Partners talk, families unwind, friends linger. In the global survey, 79% of people said they talk with others in the sauna.

blocks.html: Hot and coldPair the heat with a cold plunge or a cool outdoor shower and you have the classic contrast ritual, the Nordic way to feel completely awake.

The ritual
How to sauna, the Finnish way.

blocks.html: There’s no wrong way to enjoy a sauna, but the classic ritual is simple: heat, cool, rest, repeat.
blocks.text: There’s no wrong way to enjoy a sauna, but the classic ritual is simple: heat, cool, rest, repeat.

blocks.alt: Resting on a cedar bench as loyly steam fills a panoramic barrel sauna, The Toronto Sauna Co.

items.html: 01Heat upLet the sauna reach 80–90°C. Rinse off, then settle onto the bench for 10–15 minutes. The upper bench is hotter; start low if you’re new.
items.text: 01Heat upLet the sauna reach 80–90°C. Rinse off, then settle onto the bench for 10–15 minutes. The upper bench is hotter; start low if you’re new.

items.html: 02Add löylyLadle a little water onto the hot rocks for a burst of soft steam. It makes the heat feel deeper without raising the temperature much.
items.text: 02Add löylyLadle a little water onto the hot rocks for a burst of soft steam. It makes the heat feel deeper without raising the temperature much.

items.html: 03Cool downStep out into fresh air, take a cool shower or, if you’re used to it, a quick cold plunge.
items.text: 03Cool downStep out into fresh air, take a cool shower or, if you’re used to it, a quick cold plunge.

items.html: 04RestSit or lie down for 10 minutes and let your heart rate settle. Have some water.
items.text: 04RestSit or lie down for 10 minutes and let your heart rate settle. Have some water.

items.html: 05RepeatMost people do two or three rounds. Finish with a final rinse and an early night: you’ll sleep like a stone.
items.text: 05RepeatMost people do two or three rounds. Finish with a final rinse and an early night: you’ll sleep like a stone.

blocks.text: Good to know
Sauna sensibly.

items.html: Drink water before and after. You’ll sweat more than you think.
items.text: Drink water before and after. You’ll sweat more than you think.

items.html: Skip the alcohol. In a Swedish review of sauna deaths, about half of the people involved had been drinking.
items.text: Skip the alcohol. In a Swedish review of sauna deaths, about half of the people involved had been drinking.

items.html: Talk to your doctor first if you have a heart condition, low or high blood pressure, are pregnant, or take medication that affects heat tolerance.
items.text: Talk to your doctor first if you have a heart condition, low or high blood pressure, are pregnant, or take medication that affects heat tolerance.

items.html: Listen to your body. Leave whenever you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, and supervise children closely.
items.text: Listen to your body. Leave whenever you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, and supervise children closely.
